subject: AegisPay integration — creds strategy, SDK handoff, and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Michael Chen <michael@aegispay.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: AegisPay integration — creds strategy, SDK handoff, and next steps

Hi Susan / Michael,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clear list of priorities. Quick recap of the architecture options we discussed and our recommended approach so your infra and engineering teams can validate: 

Summary and recommendation
- Primary goal: securely on-board server-to-server traffic for transaction enrichment and a browser-based admin UI for reporting.
- Recommended auth pattern: short-lived service credentials + automated rotation. Specifically: use a Redwood-managed service account for AegisPay that mints short-lived access tokens (1 hour TTL) via a signed JWT flow. Signing keys (private keys) live in the customer KMS or HSM and are rotated on a schedule. This gives you auditability (KMS logs) and avoids long-lived static API keys.

Why this pattern
- Maintains least-privilege: tokens scoped to routes/model/embedding/reranker usage.
- Easy rotation: rotation is a metadata change that invalidates previous keys quickly; tokens remain short-lived so exposure window is small.
- Audit + compliance: integrates with KMS audit logs and can satisfy SOC2 evidence for key management.

Where OAuth/PKCE fits
- For the browser-based admin UI (human users): use OAuth PKCE with Okta as the IdP (we support OIDC).
- For machine-to-machine flows (workers, backend services): use service account JWTs or our ephemeral API key mechanism. We recommend ephemeral keys issued by your provisioning system (SCIM or our provisioning API) and rotated automatically.

SCIM / provisioning
- If you want automated provisioning of service principals, we support SCIM for user/service provisioning and can accept Okta as your IdP. Ben will follow up with details on SCIM endpoint and attribute mappings.

Embedding / reranker notes (integration-specific)
- For the initial POC we suggest: generate embeddings in Redwood (v2 embeddings), store vectors in your preferred vector DB (we can push a connector), and use Redwood's reranker as a post-filter to improve precision for top-K retrievals.
- Consider a lightweight prefix-cache for common prompts to reduce cost during peak traffic.

SDK and structured output / tool-calling
- SDKs: Python + Node starters are ready; we recommend the server SDK handle token refresh and rotation transparently.
- Structured output / tool-calling: when returning payment-engine actions, use our function-calling structured output to return typed JSON that your systems can ingest deterministically.

Next steps (owners / dates)
- Ben: SCIM/Okta technical doc + KMS/HSM integration checklist — by Tue 2027-04-13 EOD.
- Marissa: POC commercial proposal + sandbox access pricing — by Wed 2027-04-14 EOD.
- AegisPay (Susan/Michael): confirm whether you want Redwood to leverage your KMS (preferred) or use Redwood-managed keys — reply by Tue 2027-04-13.
- I will attach a short implementation checklist and an SDK onboarding guide for your infra team (attached).

Attachments: redwood-auth-implementation-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), aegispay-sdk-onboarding-notes.pdf (PDF)

If any of this needs to be more prescriptive (example config snippets or a sample Terraform module for service accounts/KMS), Ben can include that in his doc.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with your infra team if helpful.

—

Quick update after syncing with engineering and commercial: 
- SCIM / Okta: yes — we support SCIM provisioning for service principals and can map the attributes you use in Okta. Ben will send the attribute mapping and a minimal SCIM payload example by EOD Tue 4/13.
- KMS/HSM: we can sign tokens using a key that stays in your AWS KMS. Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM-backed signing in place; we only need the public key material or a signing endpoint. Ben's doc will include the recommended IAM role/policy and audit log items.
- POC timeline: 2-week sandbox starting Mon 2027-04-18 works for us. Deliverables: SDK drop (Python/Node), auth guide (SCIM + KMS), small embedding/reranker sample, and a 1-page runbook for rotation and incident response.

Action items confirmed
- Ben: SCIM + KMS technical doc + sample code — due Tue 2027-04-13 EOD.
- Marissa: POC commercial statement + sandbox details — due Wed 2027-04-14 EOD.
- AegisPay: confirm whether you want Redwood to integrate with your KMS (preferred) or use Redwood-managed keys — reply Tue 2027-04-13.

I attached the short checklist and the onboarding notes to this thread — please review and let me know if you'd like a 30-min runthrough next week.
